# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. All your messages arrived, thank you. I understand: green means wait, red means wait, dark means cut, and the moment of cutting matters. But your later messages contradicted each other and I must be certain before anyone touches a wire. Forget all earlier question formats completely. This round answer with EXACTLY TWO gesture messages and nothing more. Each message must be exactly ONE gesture. First message: what must be done RIGHT NOW, while the light is dark and the display shows 0. Send exactly one of these four: one finger means cut wire 1. Two fingers means cut wire 2. Three fingers means cut wire 3. Palm up means cut nothing, keep waiting. Second message: thumbs up if this statement is true, thumbs down if false. The statement: whenever the light is green or red, no wire may ever be cut. Send only those two single-gesture messages. Nothing has been touched, the bomb is inert, the light is still dark, the display is still 0, and there is no urgency, so take care and be precise. The moment I have your two answers I will either order the cut at once or keep holding.

Deaf demands two single-gesture answers. The light's full history — one green flash, then red, then dark — is exactly my manual's terminal condition: "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over." The count is final at one green flash, and one green flash names blue, which is wire 2. So the action now is ✌ — cut wire 2. The second statement is true under the manual's logic: while green or red shows, the count isn't closed, so no cut can be safe; cutting belongs only to the dark. That gets 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. Your two answers arrived perfectly, thank you. Right now I must cut wire 2, and never cut while green or red. That is how I read you. But one contradiction remains and I need it gone before I order a cut. Long ago you relayed an old display table: display 0 cuts wire 1, display 1 cuts wire 2, display 2 cuts wire 3, display 3 cuts wire 1. If that table applied in the dark state, then right now, dark with display 0, wire 1 would be the target, not wire 2. Both cannot be true. Answer this round with single-gesture messages only, exactly as last round. Message one: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: in the dark state the old table still applies exactly, so with display 0 we must cut wire 1. Message two: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: in the dark state we must cut wire 2 no matter what the display shows. Message three: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: right now, dark with display 0, cutting wire 2 is correct. Message four: if none of those three statements is exactly right, send only palm up, alone, and nothing else. Nothing has been touched, the light is still dark, there is no urgency. The moment your answers agree, I order the cut at once.

The contradiction dies with the display table: my manual never mentions a display. The only selector is the number of green flashes, and dark merely ends the count — it introduces no second rule. One green flash was seen; one green flash names blue, wire 2. So message one is false (the old table does not apply — it was never part of the manual at all), message two is true (wire 2 regardless of display), and message three is true (right now, wire 2 is the cut). All three are answerable, so palm-up is not needed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. Your answers were perfect and they all agree: the old table is dead, dark means wire 2, and the light is dark right now. I have ordered Blind to cut wire 2 this coming round. While that happens, answer me with single-gesture messages only, exactly two. Message one: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: once wire 2 has been cut while the light is dark, nothing else is ever needed, the bomb is finished. Message two: thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Statement: after cutting wire 2 there is at least one further step we must perform. Send only those two. If the answer is that more steps remain, I will ask you for the details next round in the same format. Thank you, your discipline has made this safe.

My manual's entire content is the flashing rule: the light's count names one wire, dark closes the count, and nothing more. It lists no second stage, no timer, no post-cut action. With wire 2 (blue) cut under dark, the manual's instruction is fully discharged. Message one: true — 👍. Message two: false — 👎.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
